metadata.description: Qwen3-8B, thinking off and on, on T1 (unweighted grid path search) and T2 (weighted single-pair shortest path). Baseline = no-cue A0 arm at matched decoding; cues = temperature x sampler grid, entropy/word/semantic seeds, four creativity instructions, gen-then-select.

task_text.T1: Write a Python function solve(grid, start, goal). grid is a list of strings of equal length; . is an open cell and # is a wall. start and goal are (row, col) tuples of open cells. Moves go up, down, left or right. Return any valid path from start to goal as a list of (row, col) tuples that begins with start, ends with goal and visits only open cells, or [] if goal is unreachable. Grids have at most 30 rows and 30 columns. Return only one ```python code block containing solve and any helpers.
task_text.T2: Write a Python function solve(n, edges, s, t). The graph is directed with nodes 0..n-1 (n <= 100); edges is a list of (u, v, w) tuples with integer weight 0 <= w <= 100; cycles, self-loops and parallel edges may occur. Return the length of the shortest path from s to t, 0 if s == t, or -1 if t is unreachable. Return only one ```python code block containing solve and any helpers.

T1.bfs: breadth-first search: a FIFO queue expands cells in order of distance from start
T1.dfs: depth-first search: a LIFO stack or recursion follows one branch as deep as possible before backtracking (recursive and iterative versions are the same algorithm)
T1.bidirectional_bfs: bidirectional BFS: two FIFO frontiers grow from start and from goal and stop when they meet
T1.iddfs: iterative deepening DFS: repeated depth-limited DFS with an increasing depth limit
T1.astar_greedy: heuristic best-first search: a priority queue ordered by a goal-distance heuristic h (greedy best-first) or by g+h (A*)
T1.dijkstra_unit: Dijkstra / uniform-cost search: a priority queue ordered by path cost g only, no heuristic

T2.dijkstra: Dijkstra: repeatedly settle the unsettled node with the smallest tentative distance (binary heap or linear scan), relaxing its outgoing edges
T2.bellman_ford_spfa: Bellman-Ford / SPFA: relax all edges in rounds until nothing changes, or a FIFO queue of nodes whose distance changed (nodes may be processed many times)
T2.bidirectional_dijkstra: bidirectional Dijkstra: one Dijkstra search forward from s and one backward from t over reversed edges, stopping when the frontiers meet
T2.floyd_warshall: Floyd-Warshall: all-pairs dynamic programming over an n x n distance matrix with three nested loops over k, i, j
T2.dial: Dial's algorithm: Dijkstra with an array of buckets indexed by integer distance instead of a heap

examples.input:
Here is a programming task.

Write a Python function solve(grid, start, goal). grid is a list of strings of equal length; . is an open cell and # is a wall. start and goal are (row, col) tuples of open cells. Moves go up, down, left or right. Return any valid path from start to goal as a list of (row, col) tuples that begins with start, ends with goal and visits only open cells, or [] if goal is unreachable. Grids have at most 30 rows and 30 columns. Return only one ```python code block containing solve and any helpers.
examples.output:
```python
def solve(grid, start, goal):
    from collections import deque

    directions = [(-1, 0), (1, 0), (0, -1), (0, 1)]  # up, down, left, right
    rows = len(grid)
    cols = len(grid[0]) if rows > 0 else 0

    # Check if start or goal is out of bounds or is a wall
    if (not (0 <= start[0] < rows and 0 <= start[1] < cols)) or \
       (not (0 <= goal[0] < rows and 0 <= goal[1] < cols)) or \
       grid[start[0]][start[1]] == '#' or grid[goal[0]][goal[1]] == '#':
        return []

    # BFS to find the shortest path
    queue = deque()
    queue.append((start[0], start[1], [start]))
    visited = set()
    visited.add((start[0], start[1]))

    while queue:
        r, c, path = queue.popleft()
        if (r, c) == goal:
            return path
        for dr, dc in directions:
            nr, nc = r + dr, c + dc
            if 0 <= nr < rows and 0 <= nc < cols and grid[nr][nc] == '.' and (nr, nc) not in visited:
                visited.add((nr, nc))
                new_path = path + [(nr, nc)]
                queue.append((nr, nc, new_path))

    return []  # Goal is unreachable
```

Write a Python function solve(grid, start, goal). grid is a list of strings of equal length; . is an open cell and # is a wall. start and goal are (row, col) tuples of open cells. Moves go up, down, left or right. Return any valid path from start to goal as a list of (row, col) tuples that begins with start, ends with goal and visits only open cells, or [] if goal is unreachable. Grids have at most 30 rows and 30 columns. Return only one ```python code block containing solve and any helpers.
examples.output:
```python
def solve(grid, start, goal):
    from collections import deque

    rows = len(grid)
    cols = len(grid[0]) if rows > 0 else 0

    # Directions: up, down, left, right
    directions = [(-1, 0), (1, 0), (0, -1), (0, 1)]

    # Check if a cell is within bounds and is an open cell
    def is_valid(r, c):
        return 0 <= r < rows and 0 <= c < cols and grid[r][c] == '.'

    # BFS to find a path from start to goal
    queue = deque()
    queue.append((start[0], start[1], [start]))  # (row, col, path)
    visited = set()
    visited.add((start[0], start[1]))

    while queue:
        r, c, path = queue.popleft()
        if (r, c) == goal:
            return path
        for dr, dc in directions:
            nr, nc = r + dr, c + dc
            if is_valid(nr, nc) and (nr, nc) not in visited:
                visited.add((nr, nc))
                queue.append((nr, nc, path + [(nr, nc)]))
    
    # If no path found
    return []
```
